correctness.rationale: A direct two-round Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé argument proves that equality of three-bit local-signature sets exactly characterizes rank-two sentence equivalence. Incomparability components form an ordinal sum and give a union of 22 displayed signature possibilities with exactly two overlaps, hence at most 20. All 20 distinct signatures are realized by explicit transitive finite posets in the result table. The unique six-vertex-minimal mask 232 has a five-vertex structural obstruction. `verify.py` independently checks all 4,824 naturally labelled posets on six vertices and representative pair EF games.

originality.rationale: No equivalent complete 20-type classification or six-element sharp representative cutoff found after targeted published-finding corpus searches for rank-two FO, two-round EF games, strict posets, ordinal-sum decompositions and equivalent formulations, plus primary-text inspection of the 2013 two-variable transitivity paper. The final mathematical statement is not implied by the cited broader decidability result or the one-red linear-order profile. Search coverage is not exhaustive; residual risks are documented.
residual_risks: Originality cannot be proven by search. An unindexed finite-model-theory note or old textbook exercise could already tabulate the same rank-two quotient.
The 2013 primary paper was materially inspected in opening pages, but its later sections were not read line by line.
The 2016 poset-query paper was inspected at abstract level only; likely inapplicable by topic, but not ruled out by complete full-text review.

value.rationale: Determining the complete rank-two finite-model quotient and sharp least representative size in the pure language of finite posets provides a natural logical invariant and a finite canonical testing basis. The 20-type classification and unique 6-point extremum are motivated structurally and are not a routine parameter substitution or arbitrary slice.
